_note: Ready-made distinctive visual identities. Pick ONE per story (or derive a new one), set its tokens in :root, and commit. Each is a starting point — tune the accent to the subject.

editorial_dark.feel: Premium data-journalism, cinematic. Good default for serious/analytical stories.
editorial_dark.type: serif display + serif body + system-ui UI

newsprint_light.feel: Classic broadsheet: warm off-white paper, black ink, one ink-accent. Authoritative, text-forward.

neon_brutalist.feel: Bold, high-energy, chunky type and hard edges; for sport, music, culture, youth subjects.
neon_brutalist.type: heavy grotesk display + clean sans body

warm_magazine.feel: Lifestyle/feature warmth: soft surfaces, generous imagery, rounded cards; for food, travel, people.
warm_magazine.type: elegant serif display + humanist sans body

choosing: Match the theme to the subject and tone; pick the accent from the data's meaning. Record the chosen theme + accent in designer.json page_rhythm so the Programmer applies it consistently.
anti_patterns: Generic-AI look: bootstrap blue, a purple/indigo gradient hero, everything center-aligned, one default system font, evenly-spaced soulless cards.
Default chart colors (raw Vega/D3 palettes) instead of the story's tokens.
A 'tone card' audio widget bolted on with no link to the data.
Decorative stock-style images that say nothing; or AI images for concrete real subjects where a real photo exists.
Walls of equal-weight charts with no hierarchy, captions or annotation.
Hero with no clear focal point or a headline competing with a busy background (always use a scrim).
make_it_distinctive: Commit to one bold idea (a signature color, a recurring motif, an unusual but readable type pairing).
Give the page a clear focal centerpiece (the map, the lead interactive, a hero stat).
Use real-world texture (photos, embeds, maps) so it feels reported, not synthesized.
Vary rhythm and centerpiece between stories so outputs don't look templated.
